claim: Tissue engineering strategies predominantly rely on the production of living substitutes, whereby implanted cells actively participate in the regenerative process.
source: Tissue engineering strategies predominantly rely on the production of living substitutes, whereby implanted cells actively participate in the regenerative process.
evidence: This is a general statement about tissue engineering strategies presented in the abstract without specific experimental data or citations in this sentence.

claim: The patient-specific performance of engineered tissues poses serious concerns on their clinical translation ability.
source: Beyond cost and delayed graft availability, the patient-specific performance of engineered tissues poses serious concerns on their clinical translation ability.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about challenges in tissue engineering translation.

claim: The regenerative capacity of eECMs solely relies on the preservation of the eECM structure and embedded signals to instruct an endogenous repair.
source: Here, the regenerative capacity solely relies on the preservation of the eECM structure and embedded signals to instruct an endogenous repair.
evidence: This is a conceptual statement about how eECMs function, based on the authors' understanding of the field.

claim: Custom human stem cell lines can be exploited for eECM manufacturing.
source: We recently described the possibility to exploit custom human stem cell lines for eECM manufacturing.
evidence: This refers to the authors' previous work, implicitly citing their own prior research.

claim: The availability of cell lines opened avenues for the design of tailored eECMs by applying dedicated genetic tools.
source: In addition to the conferred standardization, the availability of such cell lines opened avenues for the design of tailored eECMs by applying dedicated genetic tools.
evidence: This is an inference about the potential applications enabled by cell line availability.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 can be exploited as a high precision system for editing the composition and function of eECMs.
source: In this study, we demonstrated the exploitation of CRISPR/Cas9 as a high precision system for editing the composition and function of eECMs.
evidence: This is the main claim of the study, supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Human mesenchymal stromal/stem cell (hMSC) lines were modified to knock out vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and Runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2).
source: Human mesenchymal stromal/stem cell (hMSC) lines were modified to knock out vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and Runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) and assessed for their capacity to generate osteoinductive cartilage matrices.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study, supported by data in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: The successful editing of hMSCs led to targeted VEGF and RUNX2-knockout cartilage eECMs.
source: We report the successful editing of hMSCs, subsequently leading to targeted VEGF and RUNX2-knockout cartilage eECMs.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results shown in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: VEGF-knockout eECMs retained full capacity to instruct ectopic endochondral ossification despite the absence of VEGF.
source: Despite the absence of VEGF, eECMs retained full capacity to instruct ectopic endochondral ossification.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2 showing bone formation in VEGF-knockout samples.

claim: RUNX2-edited eECMs exhibited impaired hypertrophy.
source: Conversely, RUNX2-edited eECMs exhibited impaired hypertrophy, reduced ectopic ossification, and superior cartilage repair in a rat osteochondral defect.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3 showing reduced COLX expression.

claim: RUNX2-edited eECMs exhibited reduced ectopic ossification.
source: Conversely, RUNX2-edited eECMs exhibited impaired hypertrophy, reduced ectopic ossification, and superior cartilage repair in a rat osteochondral defect.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4 showing reduced bone formation.

claim: RUNX2-edited eECMs exhibited superior cartilage repair in a rat osteochondral defect.
source: Conversely, RUNX2-edited eECMs exhibited impaired hypertrophy, reduced ectopic ossification, and superior cartilage repair in a rat osteochondral defect.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5 showing improved cartilage regeneration.

claim: ECMs are complex networks of proteins providing tissue structural and mechanical support.
source: Extracellular matrices (ECMs) are complex networks of proteins not only providing tissue structural and mechanical support, but also acting as growth factor storing and presenting entities (Bonnans et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: ECMs act as growth factor storing and presenting entities.
source: Extracellular matrices (ECMs) are complex networks of proteins not only providing tissue structural and mechanical support, but also acting as growth factor storing and presenting entities (Bonnans et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: ECMs are receiving increasing attention in tissue engineering as templates capable of guiding homeostasis, remodeling, and regenerative processes.
source: As such, ECMs are receiving increasing attention in tissue engineering as templates capable of guiding homeostasis, remodeling, and regenerative processes (Hussey et al., 2018; Fattahi et al., 2022; Mouw et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations indicating a trend in the field.

claim: Native ECMs can be derived from native tissue or organs by applying a decellularization step which effectively removes the cellular fraction.
source: ECMs can be derived from native tissue or organs (native ECMs [nECMs]) by applying a decellularization step which effectively removes the cellular fraction.
evidence: This describes a standard procedure in the field, representing established knowledge.

claim: Native ECMs are commonly used as biomaterials in regenerative medicine.
source: The resulting nECMs are commonly used as biomaterials in regenerative medicine (Assunção et al., 2020; Hinderer et al., 2016), offering a natural biocompatible structure.
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: Native ECMs offer a natural biocompatible structure.
source: The resulting nECMs are commonly used as biomaterials in regenerative medicine (Assunção et al., 2020; Hinderer et al., 2016), offering a natural biocompatible structure.
evidence: This is established knowledge about nECMs supported by citations.

claim: Native ECMs suffer from substantial batch-to-batch variation with their properties being largely affected by the tissue source and the decellularization process.
source: However, they suffer from substantial batch-to-batch variation with their properties being largely affected by the tissue source and the decellularization process (Assunção et al., 2020; Hinderer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a known limitation of nECMs supported by citations.

claim: The composition of native ECMs cannot be tailored to specific needs.
source: Importantly, while displaying a high level of biological complexity and fidelity, the composition of nECMs cannot be tailored to specific needs.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of native ECMs.

claim: Synthetic ECMs are tunable materials predominantly composed of biopolymers such as poly(lactic acid), poly(glycolic acid), poly(lactic co-glycolic acid), and poly(ethylene glycol).
source: These tunable materials are predominantly composed of biopolymers such as poly(lactic acid), poly(glycolic acid), poly(lactic co-glycolic acid), and poly(ethylene glycol), which can be functionalized with bioactive substances such as peptides, growth factors, or enzymes (Fattahi et al., 2022; Tang et al., 2021; Gao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about synthetic ECMs supported by citations.

claim: Synthetic ECMs can be functionalized with bioactive substances such as peptides, growth factors, or enzymes.
source: These tunable materials are predominantly composed of biopolymers such as poly(lactic acid), poly(glycolic acid), poly(lactic co-glycolic acid), and poly(ethylene glycol), which can be functionalized with bioactive substances such as peptides, growth factors, or enzymes (Fattahi et al., 2022; Tang et al., 2021; Gao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about synthetic ECMs supported by citations.

claim: The modulation of synthetic ECM composition and chemistry offers precise control over their mechanical properties, degradability, and temporal release of instructive molecules toward improved tissue repair.
source: The possible modulation of sECM's composition and chemistry offers precise control over their mechanical properties, degradability, and temporal release of instructive molecules toward improved tissue repair.
evidence: This is an inference about the advantages of synthetic ECMs based on their tunable nature.

claim: The structure and function of synthetic ECMs remain simplified compared to their native counterpart.
source: Despite holding great promises, their structure and function remain simplified compared to their native counterpart (Filippi et al., 2020; Reddy et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a known limitation of synthetic ECMs supported by citations.

claim: Engineered ECMs result from the exploitation of stem/progenitor populations capable of depositing ECMs under specific in vitro culture conditions.
source: Those result from the exploitation of stem/progenitor populations capable of depositing ECMs under specific in vitro culture conditions (Decaris and Leach, 2011; Harvestine et al., 2018; Hoch et al., 2016; Haumer et al., 2018), which can be subsequently isolated from the cellular fraction and exploited as a cell-laid product.
evidence: This describes the approach for generating eECMs, supported by citations.

claim: Engineered ECMs can be subsequently isolated from the cellular fraction and exploited as a cell-laid product.
source: Those result from the exploitation of stem/progenitor populations capable of depositing ECMs under specific in vitro culture conditions (Decaris and Leach, 2011; Harvestine et al., 2018; Hoch et al., 2016; Haumer et al., 2018), which can be subsequently isolated from the cellular fraction and exploited as a cell-laid product.
evidence: This describes the processing of eECMs, supported by citations.

claim: Early eECM studies using primary cells exhibited variable performance associated with inter-donor variability.
source: Early studies were conducted using eECM derived from primary cells, exhibiting variable performance associated with the inter-donor variability (Sadr et al., 2012; Prewitz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The production of eECMs can be standardized through the engineering of dedicated human mesenchymal stromal/stem cell lines.
source: Most recently, we demonstrated the possibility to standardize the production of eECMs through the engineering of dedicated human mesenchymal stromal/stem cell (hMSC) lines (Bourgine et al., 2017).
evidence: This refers to the authors' previous work, supported by a citation.

claim: The MSOD-B line offers the generation of eECMs in the form of human cartilage templates.
source: Precisely, the mesenchymal sword of Damocles bone morphogenetic type-2 (MSOD-B) line offered the generation of eECMs in the form of human cartilage templates (Pigeot et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: MSOD-B cartilage templates can be devitalized, lyophilized, and stored as an off-the-shelf tissue.
source: Those cartilage templates can be further devitalized, lyophilized, and stored as an off-the-shelf tissue, retaining remarkable bone formation capacity by instructing endochondral ossification (Grigoryan et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Lyophilized MSOD-B cartilage templates retain remarkable bone formation capacity by instructing endochondral ossification.
source: Those cartilage templates can be further devitalized, lyophilized, and stored as an off-the-shelf tissue, retaining remarkable bone formation capacity by instructing endochondral ossification (Grigoryan et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The exploitation of cell lines as an unlimited cell source for eECM generation offers unprecedented standardization in graft production and performance.
source: The exploitation of cell lines as an unlimited cell source for eECM generation offers unprecedented standardization in graft production and performance.
evidence: This is an inference about the advantages of using cell lines.

claim: Cell lines consist of a robust cellular platform facilitating their further genetic engineering.
source: Meanwhile, it also consists of a robust cellular platform facilitating their further genetic engineering, to achieve the production of eECMs tailored in composition and function.
evidence: This is an inference about the advantages of cell lines for genetic engineering.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 appears as a versatile and efficient gene-editing tool.
source: Toward this objective, CRISPR/Cas9 appears as a versatile and efficient gene-editing tool.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CRISPR/Cas9 technology.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 has been extensively used for genetic screening or disease modeling.
source: While this technology has been extensively used for genetic screening or disease modeling (Golchin et al., 2020; Hazrati et al., 2022; Geurts and Clevers, 2023), the possibility to edit hMSCs and study the compositional impact on deposited eECMs has not been investigated so far.
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: The possibility to edit hMSCs and study the compositional impact on deposited eECMs has not been investigated prior to this study.
source: While this technology has been extensively used for genetic screening or disease modeling (Golchin et al., 2020; Hazrati et al., 2022; Geurts and Clevers, 2023), the possibility to edit hMSCs and study the compositional impact on deposited eECMs has not been investigated so far.
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: VEGF is a known master regulator of angiogenesis.
source: VEGF is a known master regulator of angiogenesis (Hu and Olsen, 2016) and a key mediator of endochondral ossification.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: VEGF is a key mediator of endochondral ossification.
source: VEGF is a known master regulator of angiogenesis (Hu and Olsen, 2016) and a key mediator of endochondral ossification.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes highly express VEGF, prompting vasculature invasion and subsequent osteoprogenitor recruitment.
source: When reaching hypertrophy, chondrocytes highly express VEGF, prompting vasculature invasion and subsequent osteoprogenitor recruitment.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the role of VEGF in endochondral ossification.

claim: VEGF expression by hypertrophic chondrocytes is essential for cartilage template remodeling into bone and bone marrow.
source: This was proven to be essential for cartilage template remodeling into bone and bone marrow (Duda et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to relevant literature.

claim: Out of 163 single MSOD-B clones transfected with VEGF gRNAs, 14 could be successfully expanded (8.5%).
source: Out of 163 single clones, 14 could be successfully expanded (8.5 %).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: From successfully expanded VEGF-targeted clones, five were retrieved from gRNA 1.1, six from gRNA 1.3, and three from gRNA 8.1.
source: From these clones, five were retrieved from the gRNA 1.1, six from gRNA 1.3, and three from gRNA 8.1.
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: Non-edited MSOD-B cells secreted 5000 pg/mL of VEGF as detected by ELISA.
source: In non-edited cells (MSOD-B, control), 5000 pg/mL were secreted and detected by ELISA.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Two VEGF-edited clones exhibited undetectable levels of VEGF by ELISA.
source: However, two clones exhibited undetectable levels of VEGF, both resulting from the gRNA targeting the Exon1 of the VEGF gene.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The two VEGF knockout clones resulted from gRNA targeting Exon1 of the VEGF gene.
source: However, two clones exhibited undetectable levels of VEGF, both resulting from the gRNA targeting the Exon1 of the VEGF gene.
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: Both MSOD-B and MSOD-BΔV1 displayed glycosaminoglycans indicating successful cartilage formation.
source: Both the MSOD-B and MSOD-BΔV1 displayed glycosaminoglycans (GAG) (orange to reddish in Safranin O), indicating successful cartilage formation.
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: MSOD-BΔV1 constructs had lower glycosaminoglycan content compared to MSOD-B (p<0.001).
source: A quantitative assessment (Blyscan assay) confirmed the content in glycosaminoglycans in MSOD-B and VEGF-edited clones falling in the same concentration range although a lower amount was detected in the latest group (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1E with statistical analysis.

claim: VEGF content in MSOD-BΔV1 tissues was 47.64 pg/pellet compared to 552.7 pg/pellet in MSOD-B tissues.
source: Importantly, VEGF quantification in corresponding pellets validated the successful knockout of the protein, barely detectable in the MSOD-BΔV1 and ΔV2 tissues (47.64 pg/pellet in edited clones vs 552.7 pg/pellet in MSOD-B, Figure 1F).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Confocal microscopy revealed strong deposition of Collagen Type I and Collagen Type X in all VEGF-edited and control samples.
source: Confocal microscopy revealed strong deposition of Collagen Type I (COL1) and Collagen Type X (COLX) in all samples, characteristic of mature hypertrophic cartilage tissues (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: VEGF protein could not be detected in MSOD-BΔV1 samples by immunostaining.
source: However, while the immunostaining revealed the VEGF deposition in the MSOD-B ECM, the protein could not be detected in the MSOD-BΔV1 samples (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: MSOD-BΔV1 samples exhibited reduced vascularization compared to MSOD-B at 2 weeks in vivo, though not statistically significant in the CAM assay.
source: Quantification of vascular densities (Callewaert et al., 2023) suggested a reduced vessel formation in MSOD-BΔV1 samples but without reaching significance (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2C with statistical analysis.

claim: MSOD-BΔV1 displayed more limited vascularization predominantly at the tissue periphery after 2 weeks in vivo.
source: Instead, MSOD-BΔV1 displayed a more limited vascularization, predominantly at the tissue periphery (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: MSOD-B exhibited significantly higher volume of vessels per total section volume (0.523 µm³) compared to MSOD-BΔV1 (0.231 µm³) at 2 weeks in vivo.
source: Quantification confirmed these observations with MSOD-B exhibiting a significantly higher volume of vessels per total section volume (0.523 µm3 vs 0.231 µm3 for MSOD-B and MSOD-BΔV1, respectively, Figure 2F).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2F with statistical analysis.

claim: At 2 weeks in vivo, MSOD-B and MSOD-BΔV1 showed similar bone/mineralized volume normalized to total volume (17% and 16% respectively).
source: Quantifications revealed a similar bone/mineralized volume normalized to the total volume of the graft (BV/TV, Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 2, and Figure 3) with 17% and 16% in MSOD-B and MSOD-BΔV1 samples, respectively.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2H with statistical analysis.

claim: At 6 weeks in vivo, both MSOD-B and MSOD-BΔV1 samples remodeled into fully mature bone organs with cortical and trabecular structures and bone marrow tissue.
source: At 6 weeks both samples remodeled into fully mature bone organs, characterized by the presence of cortical and trabecular structures as well as a bone marrow tissue filling the cavity (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Out of 385 single RUNX2-targeted clones, 62 could be successfully expanded (16.1% efficiency).
source: Out of 385 single clones, 62 could be successfully expanded, corresponding to a 16.1% efficiency.
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: Among 62 expanded RUNX2-targeted clones, 17 displayed reduced RUNX2 expression by intracellular flow cytometry.
source: Among the 62 clones, 17 displayed a reduced RUNX2 pattern as compared to the MSOD-B control (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2) and were further sent for sequencing analysis.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Sequencing analysis identified two successfully edited RUNX2 clones demonstrating a point mutation in exon 6 of the RUNX2 gene.
source: This led to the identification of two successfully edited clones, demonstrating a point mutation in the exon 6 of RUNX2 gene (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: MSOD-B cells exhibited intact RUNX2 proteins of 52-62 kDa by western blot.
source: MSOD-B cells exhibited intact RUNX2 proteins of 52–62 kDa (Kim et al., 2020; Hattori et al., 2022; Figure 3C).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3C, with citations supporting the expected protein size.

claim: RUNX2-edited cells displayed truncated RUNX2 proteins of 32-42 kDa by western blot.
source: Instead, the RUNX2-edited cells displayed truncated versions of 32–42 kDa, consistent with the expected mRNA shortening.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: MSOD-BΔR1 tissues showed significantly lower COLX volume (0.236 µm³) compared to MSOD-B (0.81 µm³).
source: Subsequent quantification confirmed a significant reduction of COLX volume in MSOD-BΔR1 (0.236 µm3) and MSOD-BΔR2 (0.182 µm3) compared to MSOD-B (0.81 µm3) (Figure 3G and H, Figure 3—figure supplements 7 and 8, and Figure 3—figure supplement 9).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3H with statistical analysis.

claim: MSOD-BΔR1 cells showed absence of mineralization by Alizarin Red staining after 3 weeks in osteogenic medium.
source: After 3 weeks of culture in osteogenic medium (or expansion medium, control), Alizarin Red staining revealed as a marked absence of mineralization in MSOD-BΔR1 culture, while in stark contrast with MSOD-B cells (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: MSOD-BΔR1 showed lower expression of COLX and ALPL compared to MSOD-B by qPCR.
source: Quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) analysis indicated a lower expression of COLX and ALPL in MSOD-BΔR1 (Figure 3J), key osteogenic-associated genes, of interest, the expression level of RUNX2 was only partially decreased in MSOD-BΔR1, in line with the truncated mRNA reducing but not abrogating qPCR primers binding probability.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: MSOD-BΔR1 samples showed significantly lower BV/TV at 2 weeks (7.01%) compared to MSOD-B (16.46%).
source: Subsequent quantifications confirmed these observations with a clear reduction in BV/TV as early as week 2 (16.46% in MSOD-B and 7.01% in MSOD-BΔR1) and persisting at week 6 (20.03% in MSOD-B and 4.25% in MSOD-BΔR1) (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4B with statistical analysis.

claim: MSOD-BΔR1 samples showed significantly lower BV/TV at 6 weeks (4.25%) compared to MSOD-B (20.03%).
source: Subsequent quantifications confirmed these observations with a clear reduction in BV/TV as early as week 2 (16.46% in MSOD-B and 7.01% in MSOD-BΔR1) and persisting at week 6 (20.03% in MSOD-B and 4.25% in MSOD-BΔR1) (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4B with statistical analysis.

claim: MSOD-BΔR1 samples displayed only partial maturation with limited presence of bone and bone marrow at 6 weeks in vivo.
source: As anticipated, MSOD-B tissues underwent full remodeling after 6 weeks in vivo. In sharp contrast, the MSOD-BΔR1 only displayed a partial maturation with limited presence of bone and bone marrow.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Decellularization reduced DNA content by 98.1% in MSOD-B constructs and 97.8% in MSOD-BΔR1 constructs.
source: Post-decellularization, the DNA content was significantly reduced to around 540 ng/pellet for Runx2-modified constructs and 280 ng/pellet for MSOD-B grafts (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), accounting for a reduction of 98.1% and 97.8% in DNA content respectively indicating an efficient decellularization process across samples.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: MSOD-BΔR1 group exhibited higher cartilage remnants in the subchondral area and better integration compared to MSOD-B.
source: Interestingly, the MSOD-BΔR1 group exhibited a higher remnants of GAGs in the subchondral area and better integration (Figure 5F, d, e, and f magnification) to the host tissue.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: MSOD-B group showed poor-to-no cartilage repair (1.05%) in the condyle surface area.
source: Quantification of cartilage tissue within condyle surface area confirmed a poor-to-no repair in the MSOD-B group (1.05%, Figure 5G).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5G with statistical analysis.

claim: MSOD-BΔR1 group showed cartilage regeneration reaching approximately 20.67% of the total healthy cartilage area.
source: In sharp contrast, the MSOD-BΔR1 implanted eECMs initiated a chondral regeneration reaching approximately 20.67% of the total healthy cartilage area.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5G with statistical analysis.

claim: VEGF knockout led to successful in vitro formation of cartilage with targeted protein depletion.
source: We here report the possibility to edit the composition and function of eECM by CRISPR/Cas9 engineering of human mesenchymal lines. VEGF knockout led to successful in vitro formation of cartilage with targeted protein depletion.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results from the study.

claim: VEGF knockout impacted graft vascularization onset but not the endogenous instruction of the endochondral program.
source: Upon implantation, this impacted the graft vascularization onset but not the endogenous instruction of the endochondral program.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results from the study.

claim: RUNX2 knockout prevented cartilage hypertrophy in vitro.
source: In turn, RUNX2 knockout prevented cartilage hypertrophy in vitro, significantly delaying ectopic bone and bone marrow formation in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results from the study.

claim: RUNX2 knockout significantly delayed ectopic bone and bone marrow formation in vivo.
source: In turn, RUNX2 knockout prevented cartilage hypertrophy in vitro, significantly delaying ectopic bone and bone marrow formation in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results from the study.

claim: Prevention of cartilage hypertrophy by RUNX2 deletion improved cartilage regeneration in an osteochondral defect model.
source: This strategy was validated in a functional osteochondral defect model, whereby prevention of cartilage hypertrophy by RUNX2 deletion improved cartilage regeneration.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results from the study.

claim: A clear interdependency of angiogenesis and osteogenesis occurs upon bone formation.
source: A clear interdependency of angiogenesis and osteogenesis occurs upon bone formation (Kusumbe et al., 2014; Tuckermann and Adams, 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: VEGF-enrichment has been proposed as a strategy to accelerate or increase bone graft vascularization.
source: For this reason, VEGF-enrichment has been naturally proposed as a strategy to accelerate or increase bone graft vascularization (Largo et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: VEGF knocked-out cartilage templates retained full osteoinductive potential in an ectopic environment.
source: Our study demonstrates that VEGF knocked-out cartilage templates retained full osteoinductive potential in a challenging ectopic environment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in the study.

claim: The first stage of host progenitor recruitment by eECM is not VEGF dependent.
source: This suggests that the first stage of host progenitor recruitment by our eECM is not VEGF dependent, although subsequent tissue vascularization and remodeling may be orchestrated in a second step by endogenous cell secretion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results.

claim: Other pro-angiogenic proteins embedded in the matrix may compensate for the lack of VEGF, such as BMP-2.
source: Other pro-angiogenic proteins embedded in the matrix may also have compensated for the lack of VEGF, such as BMP-2 (Pigeot et al., 2021), known to stimulate endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and differentiation (Zuo et al., 2016; Lowery and de Caestecker, 2010).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: BMP-2 is known to stimulate endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and differentiation.
source: Other pro-angiogenic proteins embedded in the matrix may also have compensated for the lack of VEGF, such as BMP-2 (Pigeot et al., 2021), known to stimulate endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and differentiation (Zuo et al., 2016; Lowery and de Caestecker, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: RUNX2 deletion fully prevented cartilage hypertrophy.
source: Conversely, RUNX2 deletion was shown to fully prevent cartilage hypertrophy, in line with published mouse models also reporting a lack of endochondral ossification and lethality at birth upon RUNX2 knockout (Kamekura et al., 2006; Komori et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Mouse models report a lack of endochondral ossification and lethality at birth upon RUNX2 knockout.
source: Conversely, RUNX2 deletion was shown to fully prevent cartilage hypertrophy, in line with published mouse models also reporting a lack of endochondral ossification and lethality at birth upon RUNX2 knockout (Kamekura et al., 2006; Komori et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: MSOD-BΔR cartilage templates exhibited osteoinductive capacity but with cortical and trabecular structures largely reduced compared to controls.
source: Here, MSOD-BΔR cartilage templates still exhibited osteoinductive capacity, but with cortical and trabecular structures largely reduced as compared to controls.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results from the study.

claim: Only MSOD-BΔR grafts could contribute to neo-chondrogenesis in the osteochondral defect model.
source: Strikingly, only the MSOD-BΔR could contribute to neo-chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results from the study.

claim: The absence of hypertrophic features prevented template degradation and favored integration to native cartilage.
source: We hypothesize that the absence of hypertrophic features prevented the template degradation and favored its integration to native cartilage.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations.

claim: Preventing the in vivo remodeling of engineered cartilage templates remains challenging in the skeletal regeneration field.
source: In fact, preventing the in vivo remodeling of engineered cartilage templates remains challenging in the skeletal regeneration field, with bone marrow MSCs cartilage systematically reaching hypertrophy and subsequent ossification.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Bone marrow MSC cartilage systematically reaches hypertrophy and subsequent ossification.
source: In fact, preventing the in vivo remodeling of engineered cartilage templates remains challenging in the skeletal regeneration field, with bone marrow MSCs cartilage systematically reaching hypertrophy and subsequent ossification.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 editing of human mesenchymal cells has previously been explored for gene and cell therapy applications.
source: CRISPR/Cas9 editing of human mesenchymal cells has previously been explored for gene and cell therapy applications (Golchin et al., 2020; Hazrati et al., 2022), for tailoring the immunomodulatory and/or differentiation capacity of engineered cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: No studies have described the exploitation of editing strategies for the generation of eECMs prior to this work.
source: However, no studies have described the exploitation of editing strategies for the generation of eECMs, whereby modified cells are absent from the final grafting product.
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: The MSOD-B line is the only human cell source capable of priming endochondral ossification by engineering living or cell-free grafts.
source: The MSOD-B line remains the only human cell source capable of priming endochondral ossification by engineering living or cell-free grafts.
evidence: This is a statement about the uniqueness of the MSOD-B line based on the authors' knowledge.

claim: The BMP-2 amount in MSOD-B eECMs is far below the typical amount used in synthetic ECM approaches for effective osteoinduction, which falls in the microgram to milligram range.
source: The BMP-2 amount is thus far below the typical amount used in sECMs approaches for effective osteoinduction, falling in the microgram to milligram range (Pigeot et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: eECM grafts exhibit a biological complexity that has not been matched by synthetic ECMs.
source: This is one key advantage of eECM graft, exhibiting a biological complexity that so far has not been matched by sECMs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison between eECMs and sECMs.
